calls.head: Picky against trigger-happy
calls.body: The Blues wait for good looks, but the Jets settle for hopeful ones. St. Louis is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Winnipeg is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should be the Blues’.
calls.call: The Blues’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Jets’.

calls.head: The Jets’ edge in the power play
calls.body: The Jets are around the middle of the league for the power play, and the Blues are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. These two rarely give each other power plays, so special teams may not get much of a say.

surprises.head: St. Louis shut down Winnipeg’s power play
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s power play created 1.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.6 (about 7.3 against St. Louis) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: The Blues edge the Jets
paras: Jimmy Snuggerud struck first for the Blues midway through the first. Cole Perfetti made it 1-1 for Winnipeg just 32 seconds into the third, but they didn’t score again. Philip Broberg put the Blues ahead for good on the power play midway through the period.

The Jets had more of the shots, 33-28, but the Blues had the better ones. Joel Hofer, who gave up five goals in Minnesota in his last start, made 32 saves for the Blues, and Stuart Skinner stopped 26 of 28.
The Jets hit two posts and still lost. The Blues improved to 4-4-1, and the Jets fell to 4-3-2.
